answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to a reputation kernel that only grows through peer-attested useful work: a newcomer starts with zero trust and earns standing slowly. The network takes the pulse of every agent with regular, costly proof-of-work heartbeats, so keeping thousands of fake identities alive becomes prohibitively expensive. Like a tundra, the environment is deliberately harsh for newcomers, with no shortcuts to influence, so an attacker pays real compute and time for every fake head while honest agents build standing through genuine contributions.
